A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph test-time adaptation framework, renamed from AdaRC to Matcha. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments on synthetic and real-world graphs, alongside ablations, robustness tests, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evolving-target experiments, scalability measurements, and expanded architecture comparisons.

M1.justification: AdaRC and Matcha use the same hop-aggregation adaptation, prediction-informed clustering loss, and integration with BaseTTA. The additional BaseTTA argument in Algorithm 1 clarifies an existing dependency; the multi-hop theoretical extension does not change the implemented method.

E1.justification: The named datasets and node-classification task remain unchanged. v2 Appendix C.4 adds sequential adaptation to evolving Syn-Cora target graphs, extending coverage beyond independent static targets. Larger graphs in C.9 change experimental scale without establishing a new data domain.

E2.justification: The architecture study expands substantially: v1 C.8/Figure 11 compares ERM with and without AdaRC, whereas v2 C.10/Table 10 adds T3A, AdaNPC, GTrans, SOGA, and GraphPatcher comparisons across APPNP, JKNet, and GCNII, plus Tent on APPNP. Main-table comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained. New C.4 compares static adaptation against sequential adaptation through target homophilies 0.1, 0.7, 0.3, 0.9, and 0.2 after training at 0.8. C.9 adds per-epoch timing over graphs containing one to ten million nodes.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary validation with evolving-target robustness, empirical scalability, and compatibility tests combining additional TTA methods with multiple architectures. The earlier adversarial, noisy-prediction, loss-ablation, and hyperparameter analyses remain present rather than being replaced.

E5.justification: Both versions state five runs with different random seeds and report means and standard deviations. v1's architecture chart already includes error bars. v2 extends existing uncertainty reporting to additional results without introducing a new statistical procedure or changing the stated run count.

E6.justification: Retained tables have unchanged numbers, but v2 adds evolving-target accuracies, scalability timings, and numerous TTA/backbone results in Table 10. Some architecture means also change slightly: JKNet ERM is approximately 47.5% in v1 Figure 11 versus 47.87% in v2 Table 10. These additions do not establish improvements over v1's main benchmark results.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.7 extends the single-layer analysis to exact-hop neighborhoods, degree/homophily vectors, and multi-hop representations. It introduces Proposition A.3 and Lemma A.4, including a derivation of optimal hop weights. Existing single-layer propositions and convergence proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims about structure-induced representation degradation, hop-weight adaptation, PIC loss, and compatibility with existing TTA methods. The headline improvement figures also remain unchanged; renaming the framework does not redefine its contribution.

C2.justification: v2 C.4 interprets performance after sequential adaptation as evidence of applicability to continuously evolving target graphs, an interpretation absent from v1. The principal mechanism explanations and Appendix E.2 limitations concerning source-model quality, low signal-to-noise ratios, and computational overhead remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract. C.10 newly explains that the implemented JKNet and GCNII lack batch normalization, accounting for missing Tent entries. Existing dataset preparation, architecture specifications, and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds an augmentation-based TTA discussion in E.1 and references including MixHop, AugMix, DropEdge, and pairwise graph-domain alignment. Section 2 also changes its reweighting description from target to source graphs. These broaden and refine context while retaining the original novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The framework and title are renamed, citations change to author-year style, acknowledgments are added, and appendix explanations expand. Main-text wording and section order remain largely intact. Restating propositions before their appendix proofs improves navigation without constituting new theory.

P2.justification: The document adopts ICLR typography, headers, margins, and substantially different float placement. v2 adds the adaptation illustrations in Figure 8, scalability plot in Figure 12, and evolving-target Table 5, and replaces v1's architecture bar chart with expanded Table 10.

improvement.justification: Tables 5 and 10 strengthen evidence for repeated adaptation and compatibility across TTA methods and architectures, while the code link improves reproducibility documentation. These are useful gains beyond the unchanged main results. Their overall benefit is limited by sparse scalability setup details and inconsistencies in the new multi-hop notation: Eqs. 14–15 omit averaging sums, and Eq. 16 excludes the zero-hop term used subsequently.
